subject: Under-stairs storage designed to fit
hook: From dark cupboard to drawers you can actually reach: the six stages.
ig:
From dark cupboard to drawers you can actually reach: the six stages.

This is a typical under-stairs project from start to finish. Swipe through to see how each stage feeds the next.

1. Survey the space, including the slope and any services.
2. Plan the layout: tall pull-outs, drawers, and access doors where needed.
3. Choose finishes at a free consultation and get an itemised quote.
4. Panels cut to your stair angle, edged and assembled in our workshop.
5. Installed by our own team, with fillers scribed to your walls.
6. Everything has a place, including the bits that only come out once a year.

The stage people underestimate is the first one. A careful survey is what lets the units follow the stairs without gaps.

If you are starting to plan for the new year, save this so you know what to expect. More of our made-to-measure furniture is through the link in bio.
fb:
Here is what a typical under-stairs storage project looks like, start to finish.

It begins with measuring the slope and noting anything that needs to stay reachable, like the meter. Then comes the layout, the finishes and an itemised quote. The panels are cut to your stair angle and assembled in our Hanley workshop, and our own team fits them and scribes the last pieces to your walls.

The images are concept visuals showing the principle, not a specific customer's home. If you would like to see genuine finished work, our showcase is the place to look:

Note the meter, cables and any uneven floor before anything is drawn. | F2: The layout | Decide where tall pull-outs go, where drawers take over and which section stays a hinged door for access. | F3: Finishes and quote | Choose doors, colours and handles at a free consultation, then receive an itemised quote with nothing hidden. | F4: Workshop | Panels are cut to the stair angle, ABS-edged and assembled in our Hanley workshop, then quality-checked. | F5: Fitting | Our own team installs the units and scribes the fillers to the wall and floor so they sit tight. | F6: In use | Coats, shoes, hoover and the Christmas boxes, each with its own place.
